chunks: Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, linking it up through his chain to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
He said: One should not tax four things: the sacrificial animal, the burial shroud, the price of a soul (ransom/freedom), and the travel fare to Mecca.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things that should not be taxed according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies four specific items—sacrificial animals, burial shrouds, manumission ransom, and travel fares to Mecca—as exempt from commercial markup (*maks*). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on reducing financial burdens during acts of worship and social obligations, ensuring that economic transactions do not become a hindrance to religious duties and social welfare.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-102 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB), “
You should not tax four things: slaughtering; burial; buying slaves; and traveling to Mecca.”
